raw_signal: (no owner signal -- this came out of an adversarial pass against a repair made in the same run)
observations: The bank is a FINITE set: `ANCHOR_POSITIONS` holds sixty positions and no more.

`anchorAnswered` is deliberately cross-regime -- that is the `PRE_HUMAN_CEILING` owner item -- and `nextAnchor` serves the first position NOT in it. So a protocol or engine bump does not re-offer positions already answered.
Therefore after a bump a player can supply at most `60 - answered` distinct answers in the new regime, and any player who had answered 31 or more can NEVER reach `MIN_BUCKET_N` in it.

MEASURED: 40 positions answered accurately under one engine build, a build change, then every remaining position -- 20 -- answered inaccurately under the next. `anchor.n = 40` at 100% accuracy, from a build no longer running, permanently, with the set exhausted. `setAside` was empty and `regime` was null, because both are computed from the DESCRIBED strata and this record is bank-only.

The `regime in force once it clears MIN_BUCKET_N` rule was carried to the bank in this run and then falsified by the record above. Its whole claim -- staleness bounded by thirty decisions rather than by the length of the record -- has no bound on this population.

AND THE PLAYERS IT DID REACH PAID A CLIFF NOTHING NAMED. On the thirtieth distinct answer in the new regime, `anchor.n` fell from 40 to 30 and `stability.n` from 20/20 to 15/15. `stability.n[0] + stability.n[1]` is printed on screen. `setAside` and `regime` stayed empty and null.
The described reading makes the same trade and renders `setAside` and `regime.current` to explain it. The bank made it silently, because neither field is computed over bank strata.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The bank should keep reading the largest regime and say that it is stale
candidate_mechanisms.explains: That the staleness cannot be bounded by accumulation on a finite set, so the honest move is to name it rather than to wait it out.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: Nothing measured contradicts it. It needs `setAside` and `regime` computed over bank strata, and a sentence, which is copy.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER for the sentence; the computation is REPO.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The floor should adapt to what the set can still supply
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why a rule written for an open stream does not transfer to a fixed sixty.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: That reading below `MIN_BUCKET_N` is the thing every reading here refuses to do, so this trades a stale number for one the page says nothing below.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER. It is a decision about what the comparison is worth at small n.

candidate_mechanisms.name: A bump should re-offer the set, which is the `anchorAnswered` question already filed
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Both this and the existing owner item at once: if answered positions are re-offered after a bump, the new regime can reach the floor and the in-force rule works as written.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: That it spends a player's time on positions they have already given, which is exactly why that item was filed rather than decided.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: OWNER, and it is the SAME decision as the open `anchorAnswered` item rather than a second one.

design_distinction: A rule that bounds staleness by accumulation assumes there is more evidence to accumulate. On a finite set whose progress is deliberately not re-offered, that assumption is false, and the bound silently becomes no bound at all.
authority: REPO for the reachability arithmetic, the measured record and the cliff. OWNER for what a between-player comparison should do when the regime in force can never reach the floor.
intervention: REVERTED. The bank takes the largest regime again, passed through `regimeInForceFirst` as an explicit `null` so there is still one implementation of the ordering. The in-force rule is not applied to a population it cannot bound, and its removal takes the unnamed cliff with it.
must_not_change: `anchorAnswered` stays cross-regime until the existing owner item is decided. Narrowing it would re-serve a position the player has answered, and it is also mechanism 3 above -- so changing it here would answer two owner questions by accident.
perceptual_success_criterion: A reader of the bank comparison can tell whether it describes conditions that still hold, on a record where they do not.
check: `tests/shared/the-bank-reading-reads-the-regime-in-force.test.ts`. Its first case is the reachable record above and asserts the stale reading rather than a fix, so a later pass cannot read the green suite as an absence. A positive control asserts no record can hold more distinct bank answers than the set has positions, which is the premise the whole argument rests on.
next_step: One decision, and it is probably the same decision as the `anchorAnswered` item in `PRE_HUMAN_CEILING.md` rather than a new one. Until then the bank reads the largest regime and does not claim a bound it does not have.
lineage: Found by an adversarial pass against a repair made earlier in the same run. The repair was correct about the defect -- the bank had copied a rule its sibling had already replaced -- and wrong that the replacement transferred. Both halves are kept.
